rfi.title: Europe heatwave 'virtually impossible' without human-caused climate change
rfi.description: The exceptional heatwave across Europe this week would have been "virtually impossible" 50 years ago without human-caused global warming, according to a rapid study by the World Weather Attribution (WWA) group published Friday.

rfi.title: Calls for child protection reforms in wake of schoolgirl Lyhanna's death
rfi.description: An investigation into previous child rape allegations against the suspect in the death of a schoolgirl in southern France has revealed failures by prosecutors and police. The case has unleashed a wave of criticism over how sexual and gender-based violence cases are handled in France, with victims, families and advocates pushing for reform.

rfi.title: Fear of mines alone could disrupt Strait of Hormuz shipping, warns French admiral
rfi.description: The Strait of Hormuz has reopened under a fragile United States-Iran deal, but it remains under close watch after maritime authorities warned of suspected and confirmed mines in the area. Former French Navy Admiral Éric Lavault – who headed France's mine warfare and seabed operations, and commanded the navy's bomb-disposal divers – told RFI that even without proof the strait has been mined, it must be checked before commercial shipping can return to normal.

rfi.title: Paris court gives oil giant TotalEnergies deadline to tighten climate policies
rfi.description: A court in Paris ruled on Thursday that energy giant TotalEnergies must account for its consumers’ greenhouse gas emissions, giving the French company six months to adjust a legally mandated risk assessment.

rfi.title: France told to do more to protect children from human trafficking
rfi.description: France must step up efforts to prevent human trafficking and improve support for victims, particularly children and young people, the Council of Europe has said, warning that weaknesses in the country's child protection system continue to leave minors exposed to exploitation.

rfi.title: Pépe stars as Cote d'Ivoire beat Curaçao to reach knockout stages for first time
rfi.description: Nicolas Pépé scored twice on Thursday to fire Cote d'Ivoire to the second phase of a World Cup tournament for the first time with a 2-0 win over Curaçao.

rfi.title: Relief in sight as temperatures set to fall in France after record heatwave
rfi.description: Temperatures are expected to fall in France from Thursday evening after another day of extreme heat that put 72 of mainland France's 96 departments on red alert, affecting more than 50 million people.

rfi.title: South African anti-migrant groups defend planned ‘Liberation March’
rfi.description: A coalition of South African organisations campaigning against undocumented migrants has defended its plans for nationwide demonstrations on 30 June, insisting the marches will be peaceful despite rising tensions and recent deadly unrest.

rfi.title: Kenya mounts huge security operation on Gen Z protest anniversary
rfi.description: Kenyan police put on a massive show of force Thursday in a bid to prevent protests marking two years since a landmark Gen Z uprising.

rfi.title: Macron to host Meloni in Antibes as France and Italy seek closer ties
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron will host Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni in the French seaside resort of Antibes, as the two leaders try to revive a relationship that has been marked by political differences.

rfi.title: Zelensky to miss Poland summit as Second World War row escalates
rfi.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky will not attend a major conference on rebuilding Ukraine being held in Poland this week, as a dispute between the two countries over Second World War remembrance threatens to overshadow talks.

rfi.title: South Africa beat South Korea to reach World Cup knockout stages for first time
rfi.description: Thapelo Maseko scored mid way through the second half against South Korea to take South Africa into the knockout stages at a World Cup for the first time.

rfi.title: Digital euro wins key EU backing as lawmakers approve draft rules
rfi.description: The European Union has moved a step closer to creating a digital euro, after members of the European Parliament passed a crucial vote on the virtual currency.

rfi.title: Brazil overpower Scotland to take Group C as Morocco wear down Haiti
rfi.description: Brazil outclassed Scotland 3-0 on Wednesday night in Miami to claim Group C at the 2026 World Cup. Carlo Ancelotti's men started the final round of games in pole position following their 3-0 win over Haiti on 19 June while Morocco edged past Scotland 1-0.

rfi.title: France announces first Ebola case in doctor returned from DR Congo
rfi.description: French health authorities on Wednesday announced the first confirmed case of Ebola identified on national territory – a doctor who had returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo.

rfi.title: US releases experimental Ebola drug for DR Congo outbreak trials
rfi.description: Experimental Ebola drugs are being shipped to Democratic Republic of Congo as the United States releases doses of a treatment for clinical trials in a widening outbreak that has caused more than 1,000 cases and over 250 deaths, the World Health Organization and US officials have said.

rfi.title: Switzerland outwit Canada to claim Group B at 2026 World Cup
rfi.description: Switzerland claimed top spot in Group B at the World Cup on Wednesday following a 2-1 win over Canada in Vancouver.

rfi.title: Seven European countries urge ‘immediate halt’ to Sudan violence
rfi.description: Seven European countries have called on Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) to immediately stop their assault on El-Obeid, a city in Sudan's North Kordofan state, warning of credible signs that a major offensive could be imminent as civilians face worsening shortages of food, water and fuel.

euronews.title: 100,000 jobs and four plants: Volkswagen reportedly plans radical overhaul
euronews.description: Volkswagen is reportedly preparing for the most radical restructuring in its history. Up to 100,000 jobs could go worldwide, twice as many as previously known. Four German plants may close.

euronews.title: Brussels to exclude military-age Ukrainian men from temporary protection scheme
euronews.description: Despite Ukraine's martial law, some draft-age Ukrainian men have crossed the border illegally and subsequently received temporary protection in EU countries in recent years.

euronews.title: Montenegro police arrest Iranian accused of hacking US universities
euronews.description: The suspect is accused of helping steal data from more than 150 US universities over a hacking campaign dating back to 2013.

euronews.title: Iraq: Ashoura in Karbala draws thousands of Shiite pilgrims for rituals
euronews.description: Thousands of Shiite pilgrims mark Ashoura in Karbala, mourning Imam Hussein’s 680 AD death with processions, prayers and reinforced security.

euronews.title: What King Charles' historic tax disclosure reveals and what it hides
euronews.description: King Charles III has become the first reigning British monarch to make his personal tax bill public, lifting the lid on a slice of the royal finances that has stayed hidden for centuries, and confirming in the process that the sovereign ranks among the country's largest taxpayers.

euronews.title: EU ban on Russian combatants faces resistance from France and Italy
euronews.description: Rome and Paris have cited legal and technical concerns over how the ban should be applied in practice.

euronews.title: Venezuela earthquakes: bodies recovered as rescue efforts continue in La Guaira
euronews.description: Rescue teams worked through the ruins of collapsed buildings in La Guaira on 25 June after twin earthquakes devastated northern Venezuela, killing at least 188 people and injuring around 1,500.

euronews.title: 500 players, ages 40 to 70: The Italian teams keeping basketball going past retirement
euronews.description: Italy's Golden Players — men and women aged 40 to 70 — are heading to the FIBA Masters Open in Corinth this July, while scientists are quietly using them to unlock the secrets of how sport shapes how we age.

euronews.title: Peppa Pig backlash as US company Hasbro requires child actors to sign voices over to AI
euronews.description: US entertainment giant Hasbro is reportedly asking child actors on the popular series Peppa Pig to sign over their voices to artificial intelligence under new contract terms. An open letter signed by 1,000 industry professionals condemns the AI contract clause and warns of matters of consent.

euronews.title: ​​Paris court rules TotalEnergies must account for indirect emissions and tighten climate policies
euronews.description: A partial victory, the ruling stopped short of making TotalEnergies directly liable for its customers’ actions.

euronews.title: Amid shifts in energy supply, which EU countries consume and produce the most gas?
euronews.description: Natural gas demand is climbing across the EU, even as domestic production struggles to keep pace. How do member states compare?

euronews.title: Recent outbreaks of 'flesh-eating bacteria' worldwide
euronews.description: Hundreds have died in recent outbreaks of the so-called flesh-eating bacteria Vibrio vulnificus and Group A strep. In 2026 Vibrio is spreading through the Mediterranean, driven by warming seas, after silently killing for decades.

euronews.title: Tehran will allow nuclear inspections during peace talks, former Iranian diplomat says
euronews.description: Seyed Hossein Mousavian, former spokesman for Iran's nuclear negotiation team, tells Euronews he believes Tehran will allow the IAEA access to its nuclear sites as part of negotiations with the US, despite some Iranian officials saying access could only be granted after a final deal has been struck.

euronews.title: Turkey produces last minute winner to beat the US as Germany end win streak with loss to Ecuador
euronews.description: The final matchday saw teams take on both more cautious and reckless approaches as they looked to secure qualification into the knockout stages.

euronews.title: UK foreign policy to remain unchanged despite government transition, deputy PM Lammy says
euronews.description: The UK's deputy Prime Minister David Lammy has told Europe Today that his country's foreign policy — including its support for Ukraine and efforts to restore EU ties — will remain unchanged when a new Prime Minister takes the reins after Keir Starmer's exit.

euronews.title: Historic joy in Abidjan as Ivory Coast reach World Cup knockouts for first time
euronews.description: Ivory Coast reaches World Cup knockout stage for the first time after Nicolas Pépé’s brace beats Curaçao 2-0, sparking huge celebrations in Abidjan.

euronews.title: Newsletter: Temperatures rise over sanctions against Russia
euronews.description: In this newsletter: Bulgaria attempts to bulldoze part of the EU's 21st sanctions package against Russia, criticism mounts over the EU's hyped rule of law reports, and a baby makes an appearance at a council meeting in Luxembourg.

euronews.title: Japan fans flood Shibuya as World Cup draw with Sweden sets up Brazil clash
euronews.description: Japan reach World Cup last 32 after 1-1 draw with Sweden on 26 June, prompting celebrations across Tokyo. , sparking huge celebrations in Tokyo’s Shibuya. They now face Brazil in the knockout stage.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, canicule : le préfet de police de Paris demande aux organisateurs de Solidays et de la Marche des fiertés d’annuler ces événements
lemonde.description: Soixante et un départements sont maintenus en vigilance rouge pour la journée de vendredi. Onze, principalement de la façade ouest, ont été rétrogradés en vigilance orange, jeudi soir, par Météo-France, 11 autres devraient suivre vendredi à 22 heures, puis 13 autres samedi matin.

lemonde.title: Aux Etats-Unis, la Cour suprême lève les obstacles à la politique anti-immigration de l’administration Trump
lemonde.description: Dans un renversement historique de la politique d’accueil du pays, les juges ont autorisé, jeudi, la révocation du statut protégeant de l’expulsion 350 000 Haïtiens et 6 000 Syriens.

lemonde.title: Edouard Philippe cherche à fendre l’armure, en visio devant 9 500 personnes pour un apéro de campagne présidentielle
lemonde.description: L’ex-premier ministre organisait, jeudi soir, une visioconférence dans 953 « salons connectés » un peu partout en France, avant son meeting du 5 juillet. « Le Monde » a suivi cette réunion depuis un appartement de Saint-Brieuc, avec des militants.

lemonde.title: Plongée dans la longue opération de sauvetage des 30 PME et des 1 200 salariés de l’ex-groupe ACI, liquidé sur fond de malversations financières
lemonde.description: Syndicats, entrepreneurs et élus ont travaillé de concert pendant huit mois avec les administrateurs judiciaires et le comité interministériel de restructurations industrielles pour préserver un maximum d’emplois. Une histoire atypique qui permet de comprendre ce qui se passe après l’annonce d’un redressement judiciaire.

lemonde.title: Comment une plante carnivore peut se refermer en une seconde sur sa proie
lemonde.description: Des physiciens se sont penchés sur le mécanisme qui permet à la dionée attrape-mouche de piéger les insectes qui s’aventureraient à l’intérieur de ses « mâchoires ».

lemonde.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : autour de Didier Deschamps et Guy Stéphan, la stratégie du staff restreint en équipe de France
lemonde.description: Contrairement à d’autres sélections, le sélectionneur tricolore, absent vendredi face à la Norvège en raison d’un deuil, compose avec un staff limité en nombre et une garde rapprochée. Une méthode atypique qui pourrait évoluer avec l’arrivée de son successeur après la Coupe du monde.

lemonde.title: A la Conférence pour la reconstruction de l’Ukraine, les entrepreneurs polonais appellent à apaiser les tensions diplomatiques entre les deux pays
lemonde.description: Le président ukrainien, Volodymyr Zelensky, est absent à Gdansk, en Pologne, où hommes d’affaires, décideurs politiques et représentants des grandes institutions financières sont réunis jusqu'à vendredi pour préparer le terrain du redressement de l’Ukraine.

lemonde.title: A Narbonne, Louis, 17 ans, meurt à la suite d’une violente agression filmée
lemonde.description: La victime a été violemment passée à tabac par plusieurs jeunes, vendredi 19 juin, avant de succomber à ses blessures quelques jours plus tard. Cinq jeunes ont été interpellés, puis mis en examen, mardi, pour tentative d’assassinat, et placés en détention provisoire.

lemonde.title: A Biarritz, l’effondrement d’une falaise, reflet de l’érosion de la côte basque
lemonde.description: Quelque 2 000 m³ de cailloux et de terre ont été précipités dans l’océan, mercredi, dans la station balnéaire basque, tuant une plongeuse. Un autre plongeur est porté disparu. Comme le littoral aquitain landais et girondin plus au nord, cette portion de côte est de plus en plus soumise aux assauts de la mer.

lemonde.title: Israël : les désaccords persistent dans l’UE sur la question des sanctions et créent des tensions à la commission
lemonde.description: Divisés sur la suspension partielle de l’accord d’association entre l’Union européenne et l’Etat hébreu, les Vingt-Sept le sont aussi sur la sanction du commerce de produits provenant des colonies dans les territoires palestiniens.

lemonde.title: New York gèle les loyers d’environ un million de logements, un succès politique pour le maire Zohran Mamdani
lemonde.description: « C’est une victoire historique pour les locataires de la ville de New York », a réagi le maire démocrate, qui avait fait de cette mesure une promesse de campagne, avant son élection en novembre dernier.

lemonde.title: Ademe : le gouvernement remise sa réforme qui avait suscité « l’incompréhension »
lemonde.description: L’article 7 du projet de loi sur l’Etat local, retiré de l’ordre du jour du Sénat, établissait la mise à disposition d’office du personnel appartenant aux délégations régionales de l’Ademe au sein des directions régionales de l’environnement. L’Ademe avait reçu de nombreux soutiens ces derniers mois.

lemonde.title: Le procès du militant trotskiste Anasse Kazib pour apologie du terrorisme est renvoyé, après la remise en cause d’une des parties civiles
lemonde.description: Les juges de la 10ᵉ chambre correctionnelle du tribunal judiciaire de Paris ont décidé jeudi de faire droit à une question prioritaire de constitutionnalité, déposée par la défense, dénonçant une « instrumentalisation » de la justice par l’association Jeunesse française juive pour « faire taire les soutiens de la Palestine ».

lemonde.title: Avec son modèle « 0,7 nm », IBM dévoile une nouvelle technologie qui augmente de 50 % la puissance des puces
lemonde.description: Grâce à une nouvelle architecture en trois dimensions, le groupe américain promet de placer près de 100 milliards de transistors sur une puce de la taille d’un ongle de la main, soit le double de la densité du modèle actuel le plus avancé.

lemonde.title: La pingthérapie, pour échanger des balles et des mots
lemonde.description: « Dix mille pas et plus ». Le psychologue et psychanalyste Jérémy Pouilloux propose depuis février des séances mêlant tennis de table et thérapie. Un dispositif qui permet selon lui de débloquer les réticences de certains patients.

lemonde.title: L’antisémitisme de Richard Wagner ressurgit au Festival de Bayreuth
lemonde.description: Michel Friedman, figure de la communauté juive allemande, devait tenir une conférence dans ce haut lieu de l’opéra qui célèbre cet été ses 150 ans. Une intervention annulée par le festival bavarois sous prétexte de sécurité. Face au tollé, la directrice, qui n’est autre que l’arrière-petite-fille du compositeur, a fait machine arrière.

Ukrainekrieg: EU will wehrfähigen Ukrainern keinen Schutzstatus mehr gewähren
zeit.description: Die EU-Kommission plant, die Aufnahmeregeln für ukrainische Männer zwischen 23 und 60 Jahren zu verschärfen. Sie müssten dann einen Asylantrag stellen.

zeit.title: Elterngeld: Familienministerium dementiert Bericht zum Umbau des Elterngeldes
zeit.description: Als »reine Spekulation« wiegelt das Familienministerium angebliche Pläne ab, mehr Vätermonate beim Elterngeld vorschreiben zu wollen. Man sei noch in der Abstimmung.

zeit.title: Stellenabbau bei Volkswagen: Volkswagen will offenbar weltweit bis zu 100.000 Stellen abbauen
zeit.description: Einem Bericht des »Manager Magazins« zufolge steht Europas größter Autokonzern vor einem massiven Stellenabbau. In Deutschland könnten mittelfristig vier Werke schließen.

zeit.title: UNODC-Weltdrogenbericht: Deutschland ist eine der Drehscheiben für Ketamin in Europa
zeit.description: Deutschland ist laut UN zu einem wichtigen Umschlagplatz für Ketamin geworden. Zugleich steigen Konsum, Behandlungsbedarf und Todesfälle im Zusammenhang mit der Droge.

france24fr.title: Immigration : l’Espagne à contre-courant
france24fr.description: En Espagne, la régularisation exceptionnelle d’un demi-million de sans-papiers se poursuit. À contre-courant de ses voisins européens, le gouvernement socialiste de Pedro Sanchez mise sur l’immigration, indispensable à son économie florissante. Pourtant, cette mesure est loin de faire l’unanimité, fustigée notamment par l’extrême droite espagnole. Reportage de Victoria David et Maude Petit-Jové.

france24fr.title: Canicule : la France en surchauffe
france24fr.description: A la Une du 26 juin, le jour d'après le double séisme qui a frappé le Venezuela, la France et la canicule qui n'en finit plus et le dernier match de poules des Bleus à la Coupe du monde de football.

france24fr.title: Canicule en direct : la Marche des fiertés prévue samedi à Paris reportée
france24fr.description: Le bilan des morts par noyade en France depuis le début de l'épisode de canicule s'élève à 55 et le gouvernement craint qu'il ne s'alourdisse encore, a déclaré vendredi la ministre des Sports Marina Ferrari. À Paris, la Marche des fiertés prévue samedi a été reportée, ont annoncé ses organisateurs. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Sihem Bensedrine, figure de la justice transitionnelle en Tunisie, condamnée à 25 ans de prison
france24fr.description: La militante tunisienne des droits humains Sihem Bensedrine, figure de l’opposition et ancienne présidente de l’Instance vérité et dignité, a annoncé vendredi à l’AFP avoir été condamnée à 25 ans de prison dans des affaires liées à la justice transitionnelle, qui visait à enquêter sur les exactions commises sous Bourguiba et Ben Ali.

france24fr.title: L'actu en dessin : au Royaume-Uni, la démission du Premier ministre Keir Starmer
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre britannique, Keir Starmer, a annoncé lundi sa démission, deux ans après son arrivée au pouvoir. Miné par son impopularité et un scandale persistant autour de l'affaire Epstein, le travailliste paye aussi les pots cassés du Brexit, ce que souligne le dessinateur Michel Kichka.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la Fifa maintient les symboles arc-en-ciel, l'Iran et l'Égypte se résignent
france24fr.description: La Fifa a confirmé l’autorisation des symboles arc-en-ciel vendredi à Seattle, lors d’un "match des fiertés" du Mondial 2026 impliquant l’Iran et l’Égypte. Malgré les récriminations de leurs fédérations, les sélectionneurs des deux pays ont choisi d’éluder la polémique.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la Côte d'Ivoire qualifiée pour les 16e, une première!
france24fr.description: La Côte d'Ivoire va rallier les 16es de finale de la Coupe du monde de football pour la première fois en quatre tentatives après sa victoire (2-0) contre Curaçao, ce jeudi. Les Éléphants terminent 2es de leur groupe et affronteront la France ou la Norvège, le 30 juin.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : résultats, articles et temps forts de la nuit
france24fr.description: Des Équatoriens qui renversent l'Allemagne, la Côte d'Ivoire qui accède pour la première fois à une phase finale de Coupe du monde, des Tunisiens qui sortent sans gloire du Mondial. Retrouvez les résultats des matches disputés dans la nuit, les temps forts et les derniers articles de France 24 sur la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.title: Course contre la montre au Venezuela pour retrouver des survivants après le double séisme
france24fr.description: Le Venezuela déplore au moins 235 morts, plus de 1500 blessés, et un nombre de personnes disparues indéterminé après le double séisme qui a frappé le pays, mercredi 24 juin. Les secours s'activent parmi les décombres pour tenter d'en extraire des survivants. Voici les dernières informations avec notre correspondant régional, Maxime Pluvinet.

france24fr.title: Au camp de base des Bleus, une préparation sans Didier Deschamps avant la Norvège
france24fr.description: Dernière répétition avant la Norvège : à quelques heures du troisième match des Bleus dans ce Mondial, notre envoyée spéciale vous emmène au camp de base de l'équipe de France, près de Boston. Enjeu sportif, absence de Didier Deschamps… On fait le point sur ce qu'il faut savoir sur « la finale du groupe I » avant le coup d'envoi.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l'Australie se qualifie pour les 16es, la Turquie sauve l'honneur face aux États-Unis
france24fr.description: Après un nul (0-0) face au Paraguay jeudi soir, l'Australie s'est qualifiée pour les 16es de finale du Mondial 2026 et reste deuxième du groupe D. La Turquie, déjà éliminée, a de son côté sauvé l'honneur en battant sur le fil les États-Unis, qui ont déjà leur ticket pour les 16es face à la Bosnie-Herzégovine.

france24fr.title: Séismes au Venezuela en direct : au moins 235 morts, la recherche effrénée des disparus se poursuit
Le Mondial offre à la présidente du Mexique et au roi d'Espagne un terrain de réconciliation
france24fr.description: La présidente du Mexique, Claudia Sheinbaum, et le roi Felipe VI d'Espagne ont informellement scellé jeudi la réconciliation entre leurs pays après plusieurs années de tensions. Les relations étaient orageuses depuis que Mexico avait exigé des excuses pour la conquête espagnole de l'Amérique au XVIème siècle. Le souverain assistera à la rencontre entre l'Espagne et l'Uruguay à Guadalajara.

france24fr.title: Deux tiers du territoire français en alerte canicule maximale, une baisse des températures attendue
france24fr.description: Deux tiers de la France restent écrasés vendredi par une canicule d'ampleur exceptionnelle, mais quelques départements sortent du niveau d'alerte maximale et une baisse progressive des températures pointe à l'horizon. Le pays déplore 55 décès par noyade, majoritairement survenus sur des points de baignade non surveillés.

france24fr.title: Séismes au Venezuela en direct : au moins 235 morts, la recherche effrénée des disparus se poursuit
france24fr.description: Les autorités ont annoncé jeudi soir un nouveau bilan provisoire de 235 morts après les puissants séismes au Venezuela. Alors que les secouristes continuent à fouiller les décombres, plusieurs pays ont promis de l'aide. L'armée américaine a fait savoir qu'elle déploierait des navires militaires, des avions et des hélicoptères en soutien aux secours. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : les Ivoiriens en joie à Philadelphie après la qualification historique des Éléphants
france24fr.description: Explosion de joie à Philadelphie après le coup de sifflet final du match Curaçao-Côte d’Ivoire (0-2) en Coupe du monde. Les supporters ivoiriens ont célébré la qualification historique des Éléphants pour les 16e de finale. La Côte d’Ivoire affrontera la France ou la Norvège lors de la prochaine étape de la compétition.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : les Pays-Bas surclassent la Tunisie, le Japon et la Suède dos à dos et qualifiés

france24fr.description: Pas de miracle pour la Tunisie. Les Aigles de Carthage ont encaissé une nouvelle lourde défaite lors de la troisième journée du groupe F de la Coupe du monde, offrant aux Pays-Bas la première place et un duel en 16es de finale contre le Maroc. Dans l'autre match, le Japon et la Suède ont fait match nul et sont également qualifiés.

new-sci.title: Screwworm could be the first species targeted by an 'extinction drive'
new-sci.description: We have developed genetic technologies that could wipe out entire species of pests that are harmful to us. Columnist Michael Le Page says the flesh-eating screwworm is the most likely first target

new-sci.title: All known Homo naledi skeletons seem to be female
new-sci.description: An analysis of tooth proteins suggests all 23 Homo naledi individuals found in the Rising Star cave in South Africa were female, which strengthens the case that they were placed there deliberately

new-sci.title: The lunar botanist with a plan to farm vegetables on the moon
new-sci.description: Jessica Atkin knows more than anyone else about what it would take to supply food for a moon base. She reveals how to build a lunar farm and what astronauts can expect to dine on

new-sci.title: Some of the last Neanderthals were surprisingly genetically diverse
new-sci.description: Genetic analysis of Neanderthals in north-western Europe reveals that this population was surprisingly genetically diverse, hinting that inbreeding didn’t lead to the species' demise

new-sci.title: Fluctuating oestrogen levels may alter how drugs enter women's brains
new-sci.description: Oestrogen levels fluctuate throughout a woman's menstrual cycle, which may impact how efficiently a drug that targets the brain can reach its destination

new-sci.title: Hidden black hole could explain mystery at the heart of our galaxy
new-sci.description: The area surrounding our galaxy’s central supermassive black hole contains three strangely different populations of stars – but one hidden black hole could explain all of them

Integrating them without conflating evidence and anecdote is especially consequential in psychiatry, where poorly contextualised information can amplify fear, nocebo responses, and non-adherence

phys-org.title: What to know about earthquake early warning systems
phys-org.description: As earthquakes struck from California to Venezuela to Japan, millions of people received warnings on their mobile phones, providing critical seconds to seek protection.

phys-org.title: Europe's extreme heat would be impossible without climate change, scientists say
phys-org.description: The record-breaking heat that's scorching Europe day and night this month would not have been possible without climate change, according to a new study.

phys-org.title: Hospitals overwhelmed as Europe heat wave shifts east
phys-org.description: A deadly European heat wave that has saturated hospitals as temperatures soared to record highs was shifting east Friday, with authorities warning of more misery on a continent not used to stretches of punishing heat.

phys-org.title: The 'water-saving' effect of vegetation under rising CO₂ may be overestimated
phys-org.description: Climate warming is intensifying terrestrial water scarcity and drought risks worldwide. Meanwhile, rising atmospheric CO2 reduces plant stomatal conductance—the openness of leaf pores that governs both CO2 intake and water loss—and improves water-use efficiency, which has been widely considered capable of alleviating land surface drying. However, a recent study reveals that this perceived benefit may have been optimistically overestimated.

phys-org.title: Extreme heat is harming remote First Nations communities. It's time we listen to them
phys-org.description: In remote Australia, First Nations communities battle extreme heat each summer. In January 2026 alone, the town of Alice Springs (Mparntwe) endured 20 days of temperatures above 40°C (104°F). This prolonged heat wave—defined as a period of unusually hot weather—can have long-lasting effects on human health, infrastructure and the environment.

phys-org.title: Economic and environmental benefits of regenerative agriculture vary widely across farms and regions
phys-org.description: Regenerative agriculture can deliver both economic and environmental benefits for European farmers, Wageningen University & Research (WUR) concludes in the research project Regenomics. Whether these benefits are actually present depends strongly on regional conditions, such as the availability of water and livestock manure. As a result, the transition to regenerative agriculture requires tailored, farm-specific approaches.

phys-org.title: The 2 earthquakes that struck Venezuela are known as a 'doublet.' Here's how they happen
phys-org.description: The two powerful earthquakes that struck Venezuela's northern coast, killing more than 180 people, were an event known as a "doublet."

phys-org.title: Nanoparticle exsolution opens a new route to functional oxide electronics and spintronics
phys-org.description: A research team has developed a new strategy to simultaneously control the electronic and magnetic properties of oxide thin films through a process known as exsolution. The team was led by Professor Hyeon Han and Professor Donghwa Lee from the Department of Materials Science and Engineering at Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH), together with Professor Sang Ho Oh's group at Korea Institute of Energy Technology (KENTECH). The findings are published in the journal Advanced

phys-org.title: How to manage public investment in science with balance
phys-org.description: Public debt is higher today and growing at a faster rate than before the pandemic in 80% of the world's economies. According to the latest fiscal report from the International Monetary Fund, global public debt could rise to 100% of GDP by the end of this decade if it continues to increase at the current rate. The increase in public debt also comes against a backdrop of great geopolitical and economic uncertainty, which could seriously jeopardize global financial resilience.

phys-org.title: Nearly isotropic superconducting property revealed in trilayer nickelate
phys-org.description: A research team led by Prof. Zhang Jinglei from Hefei Institutes of Physical Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences, found that the trilayer nickelate La4Ni3O10-δ exhibits a nearly isotropic upper critical field under high pressure. This finding provides important experimental insight into the superconducting mechanism of nickel-based materials.

phys-org.title: Integration could be key to computational thinking in students
phys-org.description: Training in computational thinking can improve a student's ability to tackle complex problems, according to research in the International Journal of Technology Enhanced Learning, which examined both students' perceptions of their own skills and their demonstrated performance. The findings come at a time when higher education faces increased pressure to equip students with transferable skills for a changing workplace.

phys-org.title: Ancient stellar flyby may still be steering long-period comets today
phys-org.description: The Gaia mission has allowed researchers to understand the motions of stars like never before, even revealing possible interactions between our solar system and nearby stars. Planetary Science Institute Senior Scientist Nathan Kaib and collaborator Sean Raymond (Universite de Bordeaux) have found that a recent stellar passage likely triggered a huge increase in comet formation as the star's gravity altered Oort cloud objects' orbits, sending them cascading into the inner solar system.

phys-org.title: Foreign funds help make housing unaffordable, according to research
phys-org.description: It's no secret that U.S. housing has gotten less affordable. From 2019 to 2025, average home prices rose 60%, according to the Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies.

phys-org.title: Microscale hydrogel fibers could enable imaging inside tiny tissue structures
phys-org.description: Researchers have developed light-transmitting hydrogel fibers that are just hundreds of micrometers in diameter. With further development, these soft fibers could one day make it possible to use imaging techniques to detect early breast cancer hidden inside very small breast ducts.

phys-org.title: After parenthood, same-sex parents diverge from different-sex norms—and from each other, researcher finds
phys-org.description: Research by Penn sociologist Pilar Gonalons-Pons and others has shown that after a man and a woman have a child, the couple's relative share of paid and unpaid labor tends to change dramatically, with the father specializing in paid work and the mother in child care.

phys-org.title: Social media messages may help counter youth loneliness epidemic by encouraging real-world connection
phys-org.description: Loneliness among young adults has reached what the U.S. surgeon general has called an "epidemic," with recent estimates suggesting that roughly half of U.S. adults report feeling lonely, and rates are particularly high among people ages 18–29. A new study from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, appearing in the  Journal of Adolescent Health, explores how social media itself can be used to address the problem.

phys-org.title: Why old nuclear-site concrete could become a tool for trapping strontium-90
phys-org.description: Crushed concrete from legacy nuclear facilities could play a far greater role in safely managing radioactive land than previously understood. Research published in ACS ES&T Water and conducted by scientists from the University of Manchester, United Kingdom National Nuclear Laboratory and Clemson University has examined how crushed concrete interacts with strontium-90, a mobile radioactive contaminant found at nuclear legacy sites such as Sellafield and Hanford.

phys-org.title: Hidden molecular code in tosyl groups directs pillararene formation and assembly, study finds
phys-org.description: A research team at Mahidol University, Thailand, has discovered that tosyl groups, long regarded as routine synthetic handles, can actively guide the formation and behavior of pillararenes—a class of pillar-shaped macrocyclic molecules widely used in supramolecular chemistry. undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

proj-syn.title: Crowning a Healthy Populism
proj-syn.description: Although recent political mobilizations in Hungary, Albania, and other parts of Central and Eastern Europe could be described as populist and nationalist, they have little in common with the aggressive ethnonationalism that MAGA professes. Could they be a model for a new form of politics?

proj-syn.title: Why Rules-Based Orders Fail
proj-syn.description: For a brief period after the Cold War, Americans persuaded themselves that the liberal order had become self-sustaining. And yet, any rules-based system elaborate enough to govern and interpret its own operations will eventually confront questions that its rules cannot answer.

proj-syn.title: The Tide Is Turning Against Russia
proj-syn.description: With Ukraine reclaiming territory, mounting drone strikes deep in Russian territory, and draining Russia’s coffers, Vladimir Putin would do well to seek a negotiated freeze to the conflict. But there is no guarantee that he will, not least because he might not grasp the situation Russia is in.

proj-syn.title: Managing Sino-American Interdependence
proj-syn.description: At their summit last month, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping seemed to recognize that they are in the same boat. If either the United States or China tries to cripple or decouple from the other, it will harm its own firms, consumers, financial markets, and innovation ecosystem.

proj-syn.title: Who Gains in an AI-Supercharged Economy?
proj-syn.description: If AI delivers as promised and fundamentally transforms the economy, we will have moved from the current investment phase, where AI builders dominate, to one where AI users will reap the greatest reward. That is what happens every time an innovation becomes a general-purpose technology.

proj-syn.title: Development in a Time of Disruption
proj-syn.description: Once firms and economies ascend to market dominance, they often kick away the ladder behind them and erect barriers to market entry to stymie would-be challengers. But developing countries can and do leapfrog incumbent technologies, and conditions for doing so may be particularly favorable now.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Un-American Capitalism
proj-syn.description: The current US administration's openly corrupt style of crony capitalism is the antithesis of the institutional foundation on which the US economy was built. The winners in the new oligarchic competition are not those who make the best products, but rather those who are best at flattering the mad king.

proj-syn.title: Can the Manchester Model Save Britain?
proj-syn.description: Following a decades-long effort to lay the foundations for economic dynamism, Greater Manchester has become the UK’s fastest-growing region. While the Manchester model cannot be precisely replicated at the national level, it does carry important lessons for outgoing Prime Minister Keir Starmer's likely successor.

proj-syn.title: How Trillionaires Are Really Made
proj-syn.description: Some may argue that the world’s first trillionaire is a story of technological triumph and a win for American capitalism. But markets have not bet on cutting-edge technology or a company too big to fail, but rather on the idea of a mega-monopolist with wealth and influence so vast that the US government will not allow him to fail.

proj-syn.title: Cities Show How Climate Action Makes Life Better
proj-syn.description: Cities have shown that a combination of adaptation measures and energy efficiency can save lives, improve well-being, reduce energy costs, and create conditions for sustainable growth. A new partnership seeks to help mayors and city leaders scale up these efforts through technical and financial assistance.

proj-syn.title: The Myth of Global Chaos
proj-syn.description: Today’s seemingly nonstop international tumult is not as unintelligible as it seems. What pundits lazily describe as chaos is the culmination of developments that were long in the making and arrived at a time when the international system was no longer able to prevent or mitigate geopolitical shocks.

proj-syn.title: The Microfinance Debate Is Missing the Point
proj-syn.description: For too long, policymakers, economists, and investors have focused on whether microfinance actually helps people, reducing a complex issue to a meaningless yes-or-no verdict. The most important questions concern how loans are designed, delivered, and regulated, who receives them, and what they are used for.

proj-syn.title: Turning Latin America’s Resilience Into Growth
proj-syn.description: Economic stabilization has been a significant achievement for Latin America and the Caribbean, a region with a long history of financial crises. But these countries need a well-sequenced reform agenda to attract private investment and create the growth engine that will translate hard-won gains into higher living standards.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup vs. the Extremists
proj-syn.description: Germany’s 2026 World Cup team, like so many others in the tournament, shows that loving one’s country and welcoming newcomers are not incompatible impulses. Although activists on the far left and the far right would have us believe otherwise, most ordinary people implicitly recognize this.

proj-syn.title: Beyond Brexit—and Back to Europe
proj-syn.description: Those who follow only intergovernmental negotiations or debates in the media might think that nothing has changed in the decade since the United Kingdom's voters decided to leave the European Union. Yet new polling finds that large majorities on both sides of the English Channel now support re-engagement.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s March of Folly in Iran
proj-syn.description: In promoting his “deal” with Iran, US President Donald Trump has tried to dress up a humiliating defeat as a victory. While it’s tempting to blame this outcome on incompetent leadership, it stems more from the policies and institutions that have allowed entertainers and profiteers to rise to power.

proj-syn.title: Alan Greenspan’s Mixed Legacy
proj-syn.description: The longtime Federal Reserve chair inferred from past crises that lightly regulated markets, while prone to excesses, could right themselves sufficiently to avoid imperiling the financial system and the economy. The correct lesson would have been that markets require strict regulation, and that competent technocrats are essential.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Yield Abundance Without Purpose?
proj-syn.description: Work and employment play a uniquely powerful role in structuring people’s days and conferring a sense of belonging, status, and self-worth. Although AI boosters insist that people would organically find new sources of meaning if most jobs are automated, there is no reason to assume so.
